title: The Capability-Safety Tradeoff Circuit: Identifying Heads That Are Jointly Responsible for Both

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: mapping which attention heads are jointly load-bearing for safety and capability explains the empirical tradeoff from RLHF and determines whether disentangling is possible, a key question for alignment practicality.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Head-level ablation and dual-benchmark measurement via TransformerLens is intermediate. Running the ablation loop across all heads and two benchmarks is systematic but technically straightforward with hooks.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: ablating each attention head (potentially dozens), measuring impact on both safety and capability benchmarks, computing Pareto trade-off, and testing activation steering on overlapping heads. Combinatorial in head count.

novelty.reasoning: Chen et al. (2024) 'Towards Understanding Safety Alignment: A Mechanistic Perspective from Safety Neurons' (NeurIPS 2025) already identified that safety and helpfulness neurons are highly overlapped, providing a mechanistic interpretation of the alignment tax. Their work uses activation contrasting and dynamic activation patching to locate ~5% safety neurons and show overlap with helpfulness. The proposed idea of head-level ablation across dual benchmarks and Pareto tradeoff mapping is a complementary methodology, but the core finding — that safety and capability share overlapping components — is substantially established. The head-level (vs neuron-level) granularity and activation steering on overlapping heads add some novelty.
